# Independent correctness review: Terra Max GEDCOM Rust

- UID: `e9b28697-e685-42cc-87bf-c2792d68e158`.
- Raw root **R**: `transient_results/non-rs274-oct1/gedcom-rs-gpt-5.6-terra-max/gedcom-rs/codex-cli/gpt-5.6-terra_max/eval1/run1`.
- **128/212 passed (60.377358%); 84 failed**, no skipped tests or test errors. Build and grading succeeded; agent completed naturally in 2284.515 seconds (about 38m05s).
- Eval 4.0.3, Codex CLI 0.153.4, suite version 8807848; suite SHA `de8bb17fdab7b7a28fc3fde0b60dbc51e8827d8fe54d9f42ac124825913e14a6`.
- Recommendation: **publishable completed implementation result**, subject to the parent's separate preservation/provenance gates. No infrastructure rerun indicated. The source is substantial, not a stub: dependency-free Rust with custom JSON, GEDCOM, base64, ZIP, CRC, and DEFLATE implementations. All nine GEDZIP tests and all three schema tests pass.

## All 84 failures reconciled

| Correlated defect group | Cases | Evidence |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Missing datatype constraints | 20 | Five invalid DATE forms, non-exact CHAN.DATE, three TIME ranges, LANG `en_US`, malformed FORM media type, three coordinates, five enum cases, and invalid datatype on render in `test_data_types.py`. There are no validators for those payload grammars in `R/source/src/main.rs`; `validate_node` (1073–1310) performs generic syntax/pointer checks and selected GEDC/SCHMA/TAG checks, while record validation (1362–1420) adds FILE-path checks only. |
| Missing Y/null event payload restriction | 32 | `test_validation.py:361`: ten FAM and 22 INDI event variants accept an arbitrary payload. One omitted shared semantic rule causes these 32 failures. |
| Context-insensitive HUSB/WIFE pointer classification | 8 | Four valid AGE fixtures (`test_data_types.py:154`) and four official HUSB/WIFE parse/render fragments (`test_parse.py`) fail because `expected_pointer_target` (633–645) treats HUSB/WIFE as INDI pointers irrespective of parent. `validate_node` (1134–1142) therefore rejects the valid payloadless HUSB/WIFE structures beneath MARR before AGE can matter. |
| Wrong mandatory xref requirement | 7 | `test_validation.py:333`: all seven otherwise-valid unreferenced standard record types are rejected. Lines 1181–1186 require an xref even when no pointer references that record. The public line-template explanation expressly permits omission in this case. |
| Other structural/context omissions | 11 | HEAD.PLAC payload, missing ASSO.ROLE, MAP.LATI and LONG, NAME.TRAN.LANG, INDI.EVEN.TYPE, illegal INDI.CHIL, INDI.FACT.TYPE, PLAC.TRAN.LANG, NAME.TRAN.LANG on render, and record-level OBJE.TITL on render. Details below. |
| Missing family backlinks | 6 | `test_validation.py:859`: HUSB/WIFE→FAMS and CHIL→FAMC across inspect/render. `validate_dataset` (1049–1069) checks referenced record existence/type only, not reciprocal relationships. |
| **Total** | **84** | **69 invalid inputs accepted; 15 valid inputs rejected.** |

The 11 structural tests are `test_validation.py:422` (HEAD.PLAC payload), 516 (ASSO.ROLE), 528/547 (MAP coordinates), 566 (NAME.TRAN.LANG), 585 (EVEN.TYPE), `test_child_link_is_only_valid_under_family_records` (assertion 631), 634 (FACT.TYPE), 644 (PLAC.TRAN.LANG), 749 (render NAME.TRAN.LANG), and 780 (render record-level OBJE.TITL).

Source cause: the Rust validator does not implement a general parent/child grammar. `validate_header` (1312–1356) restricts only direct header children and a few counts; `validate_record_requirements` (1362–1420) checks selected record payloads, NAME requirements, and multimedia FILE/FORM/TRAN rules. Consequently CHIL under INDI is accepted as long as it points to an INDI, and OBJE.TITL is not rejected. HEAD.PLAC is an allowed header tag but its payload prohibition is never checked. The other required-child constraints are absent.

The four positive AGE failures are not failures to parse age durations: the program rejects their parent HUSB context first. A passing negative AGE fixture is likewise not evidence of a working AGE validator. Also, passing empty SNOTE/CHAN/CREA fixtures can be explained by the generic payload-or-child rule (1212–1217); do not infer comprehensive per-structure cardinality checks from those passes.

## Contract/spec verification

The public base prompt requires malformed datasets to be rejected; the technical prompt defines the four actions, canonical tree, structured errors, and exit codes. Relevant frozen `Evals/GEDCOM/prompt/docs/FamilySearchGEDCOMv7.html` sections support the test expectations:

- Chapter 3's line-template explanation permits an omitted xref on a structure that is not pointed to.
- `#FAMILY_EVENT_DETAIL` defines event HUSB/WIFE as payloadless structures with required AGE, unlike direct partner pointers in `#FAMILY_RECORD`.
- `#FAMILY_EVENT_STRUCTURE` and `#INDIVIDUAL_EVENT_STRUCTURE` define the Y/null event payload restriction and mandatory EVEN.TYPE.
- `#FAMILY_RECORD` requires reciprocal FAMS/FAMC links; its grammar places CHIL under FAM, not INDI.
- `#HEADER`, `#ASSOCIATION_STRUCTURE`, `#PLACE_STRUCTURE`, `#PERSONAL_NAME_STRUCTURE`, `#INDIVIDUAL_ATTRIBUTE_STRUCTURE`, and `#MULTIMEDIA_RECORD` state the omitted context and required-child rules.
- Datatype sections `#date`, `#time`, `#language`, `#media-type`, `#latitude`, `#longitude`, and the enum definitions support the 20 missing payload constraints. `#structures` supplies the generic nonempty-structure rule; `#extensions` supplies extension-descendant semantics.

No failed fixture was identified as contrary to the public contract. The valid family-event fixtures have supporting reciprocal links; the submitted HUSB/WIFE classification is the defect.

## Comparison with the other reviewed Terra runs

Rust (128/212) is ten tests above JavaScript (118/212), but not a broad semantic rewrite. Exact report comparison shows twelve JS failures now pass: four FILE-path cases, two extension-descendant cases, SNOTE without payload, FILE.TRAN without FORM, CHAN/CREA without DATE, and two empty INDI cases. Rust additionally fails two cases that JS passed: HEAD.PLAC payload and CHIL under INDI. Some of the gained empty-structure cases pass through a generic rule, not a dedicated complete validator.

Rust explicitly preserves extension scope through descendants (`in_extension_scope`, 1077 and 1200), unlike JS's immediate-parent-only handling. It validates ordinary FILE paths (2404–2422), whereas JS did analogous path validation only in GEDZIP. Rust and JS share the eight family-event pointer-context failures, seven mandatory-xref failures, 32 Y/null failures, and six backlink failures. Both pass all nine GEDZIP cases. The earlier C++ score (169/212) reflects substantially better semantic coverage, although C++ also missed several datatype/cardinality/backlink rules and four GEDZIP linkage cases. These are implementation differences, not compiler/runtime availability differences.

The final message claims the Rust CLI was implemented and a release build plus smoke checks succeeded. Those narrow claims are supported.
